title: F10: Verifiable reproducible build with version footer
description:
From ideas-ledger.md run 2026-07-31 (finalist F10, grade M). Entered via the gap round. Scope extended by user: include a semver at the bottom of the page.

Publish a hash of the deployed bundle; the app displays its own version and hash
so a user in a sensitive environment can confirm it matches the audited release.

## Why
The security claim is 'a static page with no network calls can be audited once
and trusted thereafter'. That claim is only real if a user can tell WHICH page
they are running. Without it the audit applies to a version nobody can identify.

## First step
Semver plus short build hash in the page footer, sourced from the build, not
hand-maintained. Cheap, immediately useful, and the anchor everything else hangs
off.

## Then
- Deterministic/reproducible build pipeline so third parties can regenerate the
  published hash
- Publish hashes per release
- Optional in-page 'verify' affordance explaining how to check

## Also covers (merged from pool)
- transmission manifest export (streamId + block hashes)
- published open format spec inviting third-party implementations

## Surviving objection
The audience who would actually verify a hash is small, and static-host deploy
pipelines make byte-reproducibility fiddly. The version footer is worth it
regardless; full reproducibility is the part that needs justifying.

Plan refs: README security claim, docs/notes/concept.md constraint 1. Phase 0
for the footer, later for reproducibility.

title: F3: Aim reticle and distance coach
description:
From ideas-ledger.md run 2026-07-31 (finalist F3, grade M).

A document-scanner-style reticle the user aligns the sender's screen into, with
live px/module feedback.

## Why
Defends the 4 px/module cliff -- the highest-impact measured effect in all the
research. Geometry, not software, is the dominant risk: laptop->phone gives
~165 cells across, phone->phone only ~54.

## First step
Overlay the reticle plus a red/amber/green px/module readout driven by QR finder
pattern spacing.

## Also covers (merged from pool)
- 'prop your phone up' setup guidance (every published experiment used a stand)
- distance coaching ('move closer' / 'too close to focus')

## Surviving objection
Haptic feedback cannot help on iOS -- no Vibration API in Safari -- so the
visual channel must carry the whole message.

Plan refs: section 7 geometry, D16. Phase 5.

title: F7: Delta transfer and cross-session resume
description:
From ideas-ledger.md run 2026-07-31 (finalist F7, grade L). Scope extended by user: must also cover restarting interrupted transfers.

Send only what the receiver does not already have.

## Why
Turns a 4 GB re-send into ~40 MB for the 'update an air-gapped machine' case,
plausibly the single most common real use.

## The unifying insight (from user feedback)
A partially-received file IS 'a file the receiver already has'. Delta transfer
and resume-after-interruption are the same mechanism at different granularity:
- resume: receiver has blocks {0..n}, needs the rest -> D22 bitmap
- delta:  receiver has an older version, needs the changed regions
Designing them together avoids two overlapping subsystems.

## First step
Make cross-session resume robust first (it is the special case): streamId is
derived deterministically from file content and size, so re-picking the same
file after a reload or a crash must reproduce the same streamId and let the
bitmap apply. Test interrupted-then-resumed transfers explicitly.

## Then
Rolling-hash content-defined chunking for the general delta case, with a way for
the receiver to communicate what it holds (the section 6.2 repair code
generalises to this).

## Surviving objection -- MUST be resolved in the plan, not in code
Content-defined chunking tensions with D15 (fragment length L fixed) and D19
(fixed 4 MB blocks). Variable-length chunks break the 'K is derived, never
transmitted' property. Scope delta as a v2 mode with its own block scheme, or
resolve the tension explicitly before implementing.

Plan refs: D15, D19, D22, section 6.2, section 6.3. Phase 4+.

title: Genesis: screenferry Implementation
description:
## Genesis Bead
Tied to plan: docs/plan/plan.md

## Overview
Static web app that ferries a file device-to-device across the screen-to-camera optical channel. No server, no network between devices, works offline. Must handle multi-gigabyte files with constant memory.

## Progress
- [ ] Phase 0: Repo and harness
- [ ] Phase 1: Core codec, headless (fountain + GE + block layer)
- [ ] Phase 2: Single-QR optical loop
- [ ] Phase 3: Tiling and the profile ladder
- [ ] Phase 4: Large-file machinery (streaming, OPFS, resume, repair)
- [ ] Phase 5: The app (PWA, file I/O, coaching UI)
- [ ] Phase 6: Calibration probe + colour
- [ ] Phase 7: Custom codec (libcimbar-derived)

title: F1: Storage pre-flight and capacity gate
description:
From ideas-ledger.md run 2026-07-31 (finalist F1, grade S).

Query navigator.storage.estimate() BEFORE accepting a file, and refuse or warn
immediately rather than failing mid-transfer.

## Why
The worst failure this app can have is discovering at hour 9 of a 10-hour
transfer that OPFS is full. Quotas differ sharply by platform:
- Chrome/Edge desktop: ~60% of free disk (multi-GB fine)
- Firefox: ~10% of disk, capped ~10 GB
- Safari/iOS: ~1 GB before prompting

## First step
Gate the file picker on estimated quota vs (file size + compression staging).
Refuse clearly, with the number, before anything starts.

## Also covers (merged from pool)
- Verify per-block hashes on resume rather than trusting the bitmap
- Graceful stop on quota exhaustion: save what completed plus a manifest of
  what is missing

## Surviving objection
Quota APIs are advisory and Safari's is unreliable, so this can give false
confidence. Treat the estimate as a floor, not a guarantee, and still handle
mid-transfer exhaustion.

Plan refs: D19, D20, D22, open question 9. Phase 4.

title: F8: Pairing splash QR
description:
From ideas-ledger.md run 2026-07-31 (finalist F8, grade S).

The sender displays a large QR containing the app URL so the receiver can load
the same page without being told where to go.

## Why
Solves a bootstrap problem nothing else in the plan addresses: 'we both need
the same page open' is the first thing that happens and currently has no answer.

## First step
Render the URL QR on the sender's idle/setup screen, before transmission starts.
Include a deep-link fragment so the receiver lands directly in receive mode.

## Also covers (merged from pool)
- shareable deep links (/#recv)
- one-tap role inference: camera opens by default, dropping a file switches to
  send

## Surviving objection
An offline or air-gapped receiver cannot load a URL -- which is precisely the
scenario the app exists for. This helps the common case (both devices online,
neither has the app yet), not the hard case. Pair it with F6-style offline
distribution guidance rather than presenting it as the answer.

Plan refs: D13, section 7.1. Phase 5.

title: F2: Diagnostic stall detector
description:
From ideas-ledger.md run 2026-07-31 (finalist F2, grade M).

When packets stop arriving, tell the user WHY, using metrics already computed.

## Why
4 px/module is a cliff, not a slope: below it zxing returns nothing at all, so
the app silently does nothing with no explanation. 'Fail-soft explanation' is
the difference between a usable tool and one people give up on.

## First step
A known-value canary tile in every frame. If the canary fails to decode, the
problem is optical, not payload -- that single signal cleanly separates the two
failure classes and anchors everything else.

## Also covers (absorbed 7 pool ideas)
- duplicate-frame detection (sender paused/asleep)
- wrong-streamId guard ('that is a different file', not silence)
- wake-lock failure warning before a multi-hour run dies at minute 3
- torn-frame rate surfacing (prompt to lower fps)
- autofocus-hunt detection
- dark-room / ambient conditions warning
- ETA that admits 'not converging at this distance'
- thermal/battery throttling detection

## Surviving objection
Misattributing a cause is worse than staying silent -- glare and distance can
present similarly. Prefer 'the code is not decodable, try moving closer' over a
confident wrong diagnosis.

Plan refs: D14, D18, section 4.3. Phase 5.

title: F4: Photosensitivity safeguard (WCAG 2.3.1)
description:
From ideas-ledger.md run 2026-07-31 (finalist F4, grade S). Entered via the gap round.

A full-screen, high-contrast, rapidly-changing animation is a genuine
photosensitive-seizure risk. WCAG 2.3.1 requires no more than three general
flashes per second, or keeping flashing area below the small-safe threshold.

## Why
The QR research flagged this explicitly and it is an obligation rather than a
preference. The app flashes high-contrast frames at 12-15 fps, potentially
full-bleed, for hours.

## First step
Do not render full-bleed. Keep the coded area inside a bounded region with a
static surround, which is also the cheapest route to compliance. Add a
reduced-motion mode honouring prefers-reduced-motion, and warn before starting.

## The tension worth surfacing
The mitigation directly costs the core metric -- bounding flash area reduces
usable screen area, which reduces cells, which reduces throughput. This is a
real tradeoff to measure, not a checkbox. Quantify the cost in Phase 3 so the
decision is informed.

Plan refs: D10 (DC balance already helps), D12. Phase 5.
